items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I told Dejan, said, “You wait ’til you all get away from here.” I told him, I sent word, say, “Tell him not to play that band swinging all the way up to the church,”

ctx.x: Why did people swing in New Orleans?

They want to swing. They go . . . They’re swinging everywhere, like I told you. I gave you the description of the send off. He going to glory. Let him go. After that, let’s kick him up. They have been pleasant. They have been sweet and nice and going about their business with the family. After the family’s gone . . . The family knows what’s going to happen, but you respect the family. But [Harold] Dejan[’s band] have a tendency today that they’ll even hit that when the family’s there. They take too much liberty.…

items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-11-18
items.q: Daniel Barker and Billy Collin and Artelium used to take him around with him, make him play.

ctx.x: Harold played piano. Their older sister played piano. I think that's how they come one by another like that. Then uh, Everetta played piano. Chani played piano. Lester played piano. And Bernard played piano. But I don't think he had no lessons. I think this from one to another. See this like uh, uh, when I was small, the girl at the corner of my house was to play piano. I used to get lined up a few pieces from her when I'd go home and my brother would catch him like that. Yeah. And I was like, uh, dear See this…
He wasn't just the blues piano then. Blues piano.
